description: The recruitment advertisement that Section 2 Question 4(E) is built on, set inside a plain black rectangle. (20 marks) — the answer depends on the exact discriminatory wording ('Female applicants only' = gender ground; 'Applicants must be Irish' = race/nationality ground), so a Q4(E) card must reproduce this advert verbatim or show this crop. description: The stimulus box for Section 2 Question 5, a black rectangle split into two. description: A greyscale photograph framed by a thin black border and floating on a wide white field. It shows a large two-storey country-house hotel seen from across a lawn: hipped and gabled roofs with tall chimney stacks, bay windows and dormers, and a long single-storey glazed conservatory or extension running along its left-hand side with parasols/awnings outside. Decorative; a card can omit it.

description: A greyscale photograph with a thin black border, centred on white. Four golfers walk away from the camera across a fairway, spread in a loose line, each carrying a golf bag on one shoulder; they are shot from a low angle so that they read almost as silhouettes against a bright overcast sky, with a dark treeline along the horizon and mown grass filling the foreground. Only question prose is clipped here, so the photograph itself is whole.

description: A greyscale photograph with a thin black border, centred on white. It shows a chocolate production line: six or seven rectangular moulded chocolate bars lying in a row, running diagonally across the frame on a pale conveyor belt, each bar's upper surface covered in a regular grid of small raised bubbles or nodules. The photograph frame is complete; the conveyor running past the picture edges is the photographer's composition, not a crop defect.

description: The stimulus box for Section 2 Question 8, a black rectangle split into two. On the left is a greyscale photograph of a Cadbury chocolate-bar wrapper: the script 'Cadbury' logo at the top, 'Dairy Milk' in large script beneath it, 'CRUNCHY HONEYCOMB' below that, a starburst flash at the top right reading 'VOTE TO KEEP ME' with small print under it, an image of a broken chocolate square with honeycomb pieces, fudge and nuts bursting out, the strapline 'Milk chocolate with golden crunchy honeycomb pieces, caramel flavoured fudge and chopped hazelnuts', and a 'CREATED BY' line with a handwritten signature at the foot. On the right, two paragraphs: 'Cadbury has launched its latest products.' and 'The stages of the new product development process included Idea Generation, Product Screening and Feasibility Study. Cadbury also engaged in test marketing.' — with 'Idea Generation', 'Product Screening' and 'Feasibility Study' each underlined.
notes: The wrapper photograph is product branding and no part of Q8 asks about it, so the crop is decorative. What matters in this crop is typography rather than picture: Q8(A) says 'Explain two of the underlined terms above', and the three underlined terms visible here are Idea Generation, Product Screening and Feasibility Study — a Q8(A) card must carry those three terms (as text, with the underlining preserved or made explicit); it does not need the image. A second sentence of the Q8 stimulus, 'Cadbury bars are manufactured using mass production. The bars are wrapped using packaging with the distinctive purple Cadbury colour.', sits lower on the page outside this crop.

description: The stimulus box for Section 2 Question 9, a tall black rectangle with a greyscale photograph centred inside its upper half. The photograph shows the interior of a small hardware / DIY shop: pegboard and slatted walls hung with hand tools, coiled hose and chain, and packaged fittings; free-standing wire display racks and end units; stacked cardboard boxes and a wheeled bin standing in the middle of the floor; a black-and-white chequerboard tiled floor; a recessed fluorescent ceiling panel overhead and a small dark sign board hanging from the ceiling at the back of the shop. The case-study prose that belongs inside this box (the Ryans' 60-year-old shop near Limerick, high 2020 turnover, new DIY chain store in the nearby retail park) is live text in the PDF and is not in the crop; only question prose was clipped, so the photograph is whole.

notes: THE one genuinely examinable figure in this batch. Section 3 Part 1, Question 3 (International Environment), part (A): (i) Explain the term Balance of Payments, (ii) "Calculate the Balance of Trade and the Balance of Payments using the data above. State whether your answer is a surplus or a deficit. Show your workings." (20 marks). The four euro figures live ONLY inside this raster — I confirmed they are absent from the PDF text layer, which holds just the title "Ireland 2023 Q3" and "Adapted from cso.ie". A Q3(A)(ii) card is unanswerable without this image, so it MUST be shown, not merely described. Working the paper implies: Balance of Trade = 72 − 34 = €38bn surplus; Balance of Payments = (72+93) − (34+84) = €47bn surplus. description: An infographic bar chart in a black-bordered box. Header bar: "Inflation* rate" in bold white with "forecast" in lighter grey. The asterisk in "Inflation*" has no matching footnote anywhere inside the panel (the source infographic's own omission, not a crop cut). The box is closed on all four sides and the 2025 bar is complete; the line of question prose below the box is outside the figure.
